questions.question: Which of the following is a major factor that has facilitated globalisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid improvements in technology**__.

__
 
• Technological advancements have significantly lowered transportation and communication costs, making global trade more efficient and accessible.
 
• The internet and digital technologies have facilitated instant communication and data exchange across the globe, enhancing international business operations.
 
• Improvements in shipping and logistics technology have reduced the time and cost of moving goods across borders, boosting international trade.
 
• Advances in information technology have enabled companies to manage global supply chains more effectively, coordinating production and distribution worldwide.
 
• Technological innovation has also led to the development of new products and services, opening up new markets and driving economic globalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Supply Chains:** Technological advancements have enabled the development of complex global supply chains, where production processes are distributed across multiple countries to optimize costs and efficiency.
 
• **Telecommunications:** The evolution of telecommunications, including mobile networks and internet connectivity, has facilitated real-time communication and collaboration between businesses and individuals worldwide.
 
• **E-commerce:** The rise of e-commerce platforms has allowed businesses to reach international customers directly, bypassing traditional physical retail channels and expanding their global presence.
 
• **Automation and Robotics:** Technological innovations in automation and robotics have increased productivity and efficiency in manufacturing, enabling companies to compete globally by reducing production costs.
 
• **Financial Technologies:** Developments in financial technologies (FinTech) have streamlined international payments and transactions, making it easier for businesses to operate across borders.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the All India Muslim League, founded in 1906?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aga Khan III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aga Khan III** was the first President of the All India Muslim League, which was founded in 1906.
 
• The All India Muslim League was established to advocate for the rights of Muslims in British India.
 
• Aga Khan III played a crucial role in the formation and leadership of the league, guiding its initial steps and objectives.
 
• His leadership was significant in shaping the political landscape for Muslims in India during the early 20th century.
 
• The league later became a driving force behind the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Muslim League**:

 
 
• Founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca (now Dhaka), it was the political party representing the interests of the Muslim population in British India.
 
• The league's formation was in response to the growing need for a separate political platform for Muslims to safeguard their rights and interests.
 
• Key figures included Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah (Aga Khan III), Nawab Salimullah, and others.
 
 
 
• **Aga Khan III**:
 
 
• Born as Sir Sultan Mahomed Shah, he was the 48th Imam of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims.
 
• He was a prominent leader and philanthropist, significantly contributing to education and healthcare for Muslims.
 
• He also played an influential role in the international Muslim community through organizations like the League of Nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Pakistan Movement**:
 
 
• The All India Muslim League was instrumental in the demand for a separate Muslim state, leading to the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
• Under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the league's demand for Pakistan became a reality.
 
• The Lahore Resolution of 1940, passed by the league, was a turning point in the Pakistan Movement.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**:
 
 
• The All India Muslim League's legacy continues in Pakistan, where it laid the foundation for the nation's political framework.
 
• It inspired subsequent political movements and parties in both Pakistan and India.
 
• The contributions of early leaders like Aga Khan III are remembered for their vision and efforts towards Muslim empowerment.

questions.question: Name the virus spread by mosquitoes that causes inflammation in the brain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japanese encephalitis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Japanese encephalitis (JE) is a viral infection that causes inflammation of the brain.
 
• The virus is transmitted by the bite of infected mosquitoes, primarily the Culex species.
 
• JE is prevalent in rural and agricultural areas of Asia and the Western Pacific.
 
• Symptoms of JE include high fever, headache, neck stiffness, disorientation, coma, seizures, and paralysis.
 
• There is no specific antiviral treatment for JE; supportive care is the primary approach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transmission Cycle**

 
 
• The JE virus is maintained in a cycle involving mosquitoes and vertebrate hosts, primarily pigs and wading birds.
 
• Humans are incidental hosts and do not contribute to the transmission cycle.
 
 
 
• **Vaccination**
 
 
• Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent JE.
 
• Several types of JE vaccines are available, including inactivated and live-attenuated vaccines.
 
 
 
• **Prevention**
 
 
• Preventive measures include using mosquito nets, insect repellents, and wearing protective clothing.
 
• Control of mosquito populations through environmental management and insecticide use is crucial.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact**
 
 
• JE is a significant public health issue in many Asian countries, with thousands of cases reported annually.
 
• Outbreaks often occur in regions with endemic JE and can lead to high morbidity and mortality rates.

questions.question: For a book of mass m, moving a distance d on a smooth horizontal table, the work done due gravitational force is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done by a force is defined as the dot product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• On a smooth horizontal table, the gravitational force acts vertically downward, while the displacement is horizontal.
 
• The angle between the gravitational force and the horizontal displacement is 90 degrees.
 
• The cosine of 90 degrees is 0, hence the work done by the gravitational force over the horizontal displacement is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work**: In physics, work is done when a force acts upon an object to cause a displacement. It is calculated as the product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• **Gravitational Force**: The force of attraction between two masses. Near the Earth's surface, it imparts an acceleration of 9.81 m/s² downward.
 
• **Dot Product**: A mathematical operation that takes two equal-length sequences of numbers (usually coordinate vectors) and returns a single number. It is defined as the product of the magnitudes of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle between them.
 
• **Cosine Function**: In trigonometry, the cosine of an angle in a right-angled triangle is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side to the length of the hypotenuse. The cosine of 90 degrees is 0.
 
• **Smooth Surface**: A surface with no friction. On a smooth horizontal table, there is no resistance to horizontal motion, and thus gravitational force does not affect horizontal displacement.

__
 
• The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Right to Property was originally provided under Article 31 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• After the amendment, the Right to Property was made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This amendment was introduced to curb the misuse of the right and to facilitate land reforms.
 
• The amendment aimed to balance individual rights and the need for socio-economic justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• They include rights such as the right to equality, freedom of speech, and protection against discrimination.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Article 31**
 
 
• Before the 44th Amendment, Article 31 guaranteed the right to property as a Fundamental Right.
 
• It provided for compensation in case of acquisition or requisition of private property by the state.
 
• The article was often used to challenge land acquisition laws, delaying socio-economic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A**
 
 
• Post the 44th Amendment, the right to property was moved to Article 300A.
 
• Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of their property save by authority of law.
 
• This made the right to property a legal right, not a Fundamental Right.
 
• It allowed the government more flexibility in implementing land reforms and socio-economic policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Amendment**
 
 
• The shift from a Fundamental Right to a legal right reduced the number of litigations over land acquisition.
 
• It facilitated the implementation of land reforms and equitable distribution of resources.
 
• The amendment balanced individual property rights with the need for social justice and economic development.

questions.question: If the cost price of a camera is 75% of its selling price, then the profit per cent is:

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (1 / 3) × 100 = 33 ¹/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 33 ¹/₃%.**

questions.question: The LCM of 56, 30, 108 and 120 is:

LCM(840, 108) → Both 840 and 108 are divisible by 12 (840 = 12 × 70, 108 = 12 × 9).

Since 70 and 9 share no further common factors, the LCM is 12 × 70 × 9 = 840 × 9 = 7560.

**∴ The correct answer is 7560.**

⇒ Prime factorisation of 56 = 2³ × 7

⇒ Prime factorisation of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorisation of 108 = 2² × 3³

⇒ Prime factorisation of 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of prime factors 2, 3, 5, and 7

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3³ × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 8 × 27 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 40 × 189

⇒ LCM = 7560

**∴ The correct answer is 7560.**

HCF of Fractions

Product Rule

questions.question: Find the HCF of 153, 117 and 405.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The HCF must exactly divide the difference between any two given numbers: 153 − 117 = 36.

The factors of 36 are 36, 18, 12, 9, 6, 4, 3, 2, and 1.

Since 153, 117, and 405 are all odd numbers, their HCF cannot be an even number.

Eliminating the even factors of 36, the highest possible odd factor remaining is 9.

Checking divisibility, the sum of digits for all three numbers is 9, so they are perfectly divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The given numbers are 153, 117, and 405.

**Method Used:**

Prime factorisation method to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF).

**Calculations:**

⇒ 153 = 3 × 3 × 17 = 3² × 17

⇒ 117 = 3 × 3 × 13 = 3² × 13

⇒ 405 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 3⁴ × 5

⇒ The HCF is calculated as the product of the smallest powers of all common prime factors.

⇒ The only common prime factor among all three numbers is 3.

⇒ The smallest power of 3 present in the prime factorisations is 3².

⇒ HCF = 3² = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers completely without leaving any remainder. It is also known as Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

It is the smallest common multiple of the given numbers. For any two numbers, Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.

HCF of Fractions

The HCF of given fractions can be calculated as (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

33 × Second Number = 66 × 11

Second Number = (66 × 11) ÷ 33

Second Number = 2 × 11 = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 66

HCF of two numbers = 11

First Number = 33

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the second number be x.

⇒ 33 × x = 66 × 11

⇒ x = (66 × 11) ÷ 33

⇒ x = 726 ÷ 33

⇒ x = 2 × 11

⇒ x = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers a and b, a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule applies only to exactly two numbers, not three or more.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators)
LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their HCF is 1. Their LCM will always be equal to the product of the two numbers.

questions.question: The amount of money earned on a job is directly proportional to the number of hours worked. If ₹324 is earned in 6 hours, then how much money (in ₹) will be earned in 29 hours of work?

⇒ 324 / 6 = x / 29

⇒ x = (324 / 6) × 29

Directly Proportional Quantities

When two quantities A and B are directly proportional, their ratio remains constant. A ∝ B ⇒ A / B = k (constant). If one quantity increases, the other increases in the exact same ratio.

Unitary Method

Inversely Proportional Quantities

When two quantities A and B are inversely proportional, their product remains constant. A ∝ 1 / B ⇒ A × B = k. For example, time taken to cover a fixed distance is inversely proportional to speed.

questions.question: The speed of a stream is 9 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 56 km downstream and 28 km upstream in 7 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time = Ddₒwₙ / (B + S) + Dᵤₚ / (B − S)

⇒ 7 = 56 / (B + 9) + 28 / (B − 9)

⇒ 1 = 8 / (B + 9) + 4 / (B − 9) (Dividing by 7 on both sides)

Checking the options, for B = 15 km/h: 8 / 24 + 4 / 6 = 1/3 + 2/3 = 1 (Equation satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of stream (S) = 9 km/h

Distance downstream (Dd) = 56 km

Distance upstream (Dᵤ) = 28 km

Total time (T) = 7 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = Dd / (B + S) + Dᵤ / (B − S)

 
 
• 
 Downstream: 56 km
 

 Speed = B + 9
 Upstream: 28 km
 

 Speed = B − 9
 Total Time = 7 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ 56 / (B + 9) + 28 / (B − 9) = 7

⇒ 8 / (B + 9) + 4 / (B − 9) = 1

⇒ [8(B − 9) + 4(B + 9)] / [(B + 9)(B − 9)] = 1

⇒ 8B − 72 + 4B + 36 = B² − 81

⇒ 12B − 36 = B² − 81

⇒ B² − 12B − 45 = 0

⇒ B² − 15B + 3B − 45 = 0

⇒ B(B − 15) + 3(B − 15) = 0

⇒ (B − 15)(B + 3) = 0

⇒ B = 15 or B = −3

⇒ Since speed cannot be negative, B = 15 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

If the speed of a boat in still water is B and the speed of the stream is S, then downstream speed = B + S and upstream speed = B − S.

Finding Speed from Downstream & Upstream

Speed of boat in still water (B) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream (S) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed

When a boat travels equal distances downstream and upstream, its average speed for the entire journey is given by (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Speed of boat in still water.
